summary: Join our specialized training on Contaminants of Emerging Concern in water resources. Equip yourself with essential skills to address modern water challenges.
lede: Contaminants of emerging concern in water resources include substances such as PFAS, pharmaceuticals and microplastics that need careful assessment. This course is for water utility and treatment staff, environmental and compliance professionals, laboratory teams, and others responsible for water quality. Participants learn to prioritize contaminants, design fit-for-purpose monitoring and sampling, assess trace-level data, and compare treatment options.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for a diverse group of professionals tasked with safeguarding water resources against emerging contaminants.
audience: Water utility and treatment plant managers
Public sector staff in water, environment, health
NGO WASH and environmental program leads
modules: Understanding Contaminants of Emerging Concern (CECs) in Water Resources
Sources and Pathways: How CECs Enter Water Systems
Risk Prioritization and Screening: What to Monitor First
Designing a Fit-for-Purpose CEC Monitoring Program
Laboratory Coordination and QA/QC for Ultra-Trace Data
Interpreting Results and Communicating Uncertainty Responsibly
Mitigation and Treatment Options: Choosing What Works
Incident Response and Escalation for Emerging Contaminants
Compliance Readiness and Governance in an Evolving Standards Landscape
prerequisites: Participants should have a foundational understanding of water quality management and basic familiarity with laboratory processes. Prior experience in environmental science or engineering is recommended.
topics: Water & wastewater treatment and utility management
